concepts.why: High signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus, opacification on right frontal sinus, and expansion of the right frontal sinus without any bone destruction suggest chronic frontal sinusitis.

A 2-year history of swelling of her right upper eyelid, discharge of pus for the previous 10 months, and an immovable scarlike node on her right upper eyelid discharging pus suggest preseptal cellulitis.

Opacification on right frontal sinus, right ethmoid sinus, and right maxillary sinus, expansion of the right frontal sinus and right ethmoid sinus, and mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis suggest chronic sinusitis.
Discharge of pus for the previous 10 months, an immovable scarlike node on her right upper eyelid discharging pus, and mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis suggest an orbital infection.

rationales.F01: Swelling of the right upper eyelid could be related to sinusitis or preseptal cellulitis.
rationales.F02: Pus discharge from the eyelid suggests an infectious process, possibly related to sinusitis or preseptal cellulitis.
rationales.F06: The presence of a scarlike node discharging pus on the eyelid strongly suggests a chronic infectious process, possibly related to sinusitis or preseptal cellulitis.
rationales.F07: Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI is highly suggestive of chronic frontal sinusitis.
rationales.F08: Opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT is highly suggestive of chronic sinusitis.
rationales.F10: Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate suggests a chronic inflammatory process, possibly related to sinusitis.
